text:
Ich habe heute weder aus Berlin noch aus Frankfurth briefe.
Meine Besorgnis vermehrt sich daher ständlich. Haben Ewr Hoch
fürstliche Durchlaucht etwas von Glenck, daß Trost gewährt
ſo geruhen Sie es doch Ihrem Knechte mitzutheilen.
Wegen Kolzig hofte ich sehr - Aber Amelang antwor¬
tet nicht. Wäre da ein Strahl von Hoffnung erschienen
ſo hätte ich gerathen allen Verkauf von Kontop zu
untersagen - Schweigt Amelang aber ferner noch den
ihm in dieser Sache gemachte Plan so muß ich glaube,
daß ihm Beym nicht gantirt; und in dieser Rücksicht
müſte der Verkauf von Kontop eifrig betrieben werden
Ich habe zu dem Ende Bernhardi herbestellt und ihm angedeutet daß er
als Pächter die Güter jedem Kauflustigen bestens em-
pfehlen und anzeigen solle - den auf diese Gattung

Menschen komt vieles an. Dem
1 könte ſelch Wesen um in Pacht ſicher zu bleiben den
Kauf durch gräuliche Schilderungen leicht hindern auch
könte so ein Mensch
2 Aus Gewinn ſolcht, ſich leicht erkaufen laßen, und dem
Verkäufer zum Nachtheil handeln, daher habe
ich ihm laßen herkommen und dies alles vorzubeugen
Jezt sage ich ihr gleich wieder fort, damit er wan
Budolf und Stubenrauch hinkommen, sie nicht nur gut
auf nimmt, sondern denen Leuten alles wahr und von
der Beſten Seite ſchildert.
Nachmittag bringe ich das was nach Südpreußen zu
schicken ist heraus - jezt muß ich meine Geschäfte.
dern ich viel vorgefunden habe – erſt aranquen
v Triebenfeld
Breslau[?] d. 15ten May 1804.

translation.en: Today I have letters neither from Berlin nor from Frankfurt an der Oder. My anxiety therefore increases hourly. If Your Most Serene Highness has anything from Glenck that affords comfort, be pleased then to communicate it to Your bondsman. Concerning Kolzig I had great hopes — but Amelang does not answer. Had a ray of hope appeared there, I should have advised that all sale of Kontop be forbidden — but if Amelang continues to be silent as to the plan laid before him in this matter, then I must believe that [uncertain: Beym] does not guarantee it for him; and in this regard the sale of Kontop would have to be pressed forward vigorously. To that end I have summoned Bernhardi here and given him to understand that he, as the tenant, should commend and represent the estates in the best light to every prospective purchaser — for with that species of

people much depends. The 1st, such a creature might, in order to remain secure in his tenancy, easily hinder the sale by hideous descriptions; also, such a man might 2ndly, seeking his own profit, easily let himself be bought, and act to the seller's disadvantage; therefore I have had him come here, and to forestall all this. Now I am sending him off again at once, so that when Budolf and Stubenrauch arrive there, he may not only receive them well, but describe everything to those people truthfully and in the best light.

This afternoon I shall bring out what is to be sent to South Prussia — now I must first [uncertain: arrange] my business, of which I have found a great deal awaiting me.
v. Triebenfeld

Breslau[?] d. 15th of May 1804.

text_english:
Today I have letters neither from Berlin nor from Frankfurt an der Oder. My anxiety therefore increases hourly. If Your Most Serene Highness has anything from Glenck that affords comfort, be pleased then to communicate it to Your bondsman. Concerning Kolzig I had great hopes — but Amelang does not answer. Had a ray of hope appeared there, I should have advised that all sale of Kontop be forbidden — but if Amelang continues to be silent as to the plan laid before him in this matter, then I must believe that [uncertain: Beym] does not guarantee it for him; and in this regard the sale of Kontop would have to be pressed forward vigorously. To that end I have summoned Bernhardi here and given him to understand that he, as the tenant, should commend and represent the estates in the best light to every prospective purchaser — for with that species of

people much depends. The 1st, such a creature might, in order to remain secure in his tenancy, easily hinder the sale by hideous descriptions; also, such a man might 2ndly, seeking his own profit, easily let himself be bought, and act to the seller's disadvantage; therefore I have had him come here, and to forestall all this. Now I am sending him off again at once, so that when Budolf and Stubenrauch arrive there, he may not only receive them well, but describe everything to those people truthfully and in the best light.

This afternoon I shall bring out what is to be sent to South Prussia — now I must first [uncertain: arrange] my business, of which I have found a great deal awaiting me.
v. Triebenfeld

Breslau[?] d. 15th of May 1804.
summary_en: Reports no post from Berlin or Frankfurt and mounting anxiety; begs any comforting news from Glenck. Hopes pinned on Kolzig have faded since Amelang does not answer the plan put to him, so the sale of Kontop must now be pushed hard rather than forbidden. Bernhardi, the lessee, has been summoned to Breslau and instructed to describe the estates favourably and truthfully to Rudolf and Stubenrauch, lest he obstruct the sale or be bought off.
summary_de: Klagt über ausbleibende Nachrichten aus Berlin und Frankfurt und wachsende Unruhe; bittet um Mitteilung tröstlicher Nachrichten von Glenck. Wegen Kolzig hatte er Hoffnung, doch Amelang antwortet nicht auf den vorgelegten Plan; daher sei der Verkauf von Kontop eifrig zu betreiben, statt ihn zu untersagen. Zu diesem Zweck hat er den Pächter Bernhardi nach Breslau kommen lassen und ihn angewiesen, die Güter jedem Kaufliebhaber wahrheitsgemäß und günstig darzustellen und Rudolf und Stubenrauch gut aufzunehmen, um Verhinderung des Verkaufs oder Bestechung vorzubeugen.
